title: X は Y です: "X is Y"
explanation: The simplest Japanese sentence says what something is. Put the topic first, add は, then say what it is, and finish with です.
は marks the topic ("as for X ..."). When it is a particle, は is pronounced "wa", not "ha". です is the polite ending; it covers "is", "am" and "are".
Japanese has no words like "a" or "the", so がくせい です can mean "is a student". The subject is often dropped when it is clear.
structure_notes: Topic + は + description + です. Add さん after another person's name, never your own.
common_mistakes: Reading the particle は as "ha" (it is "wa").
Adding さん to your own name.
Using の where は is needed.

title: Questions with か
pattern: X は Y です か
explanation: To ask a yes/no question, add か to the end of the sentence. The word order does not change, and in writing you do not need a question mark.
A question word such as だれ (who), なに / なん (what) takes the place of the answer: おなまえ は なん です か. To answer a yes/no question say はい (yes) or いいえ (no) and then repeat the sentence.
When talking to someone you often drop あなた and use their name with さん instead.
structure_notes: Sentence + か. Answer: はい / いいえ + statement.
common_mistakes: Raising the pitch but forgetting か in polite speech.
Putting か at the start of the sentence.
